expected_per_dictation.notes: Multi-rule. History (ACL reconstruction) -> graft wording replaces the native cruciate sentence; 'No old imaging on the system' -> comparison replaced; radial lateral meniscal tear -> two-slice clause used and clinic review appended. Small effusion flips the effusion negative. 'No displaced meniscal fragment.' and 'No bone marrow oedema or fracture.' stand. Bone tunnels being 'fine' and 'no cyclops' map onto the replacement text.
Normal. Radiographs last month -> standard comparison sentence. All NORMAL/NEGATIVE units stand; impression 'No internal derangement of the right knee.'

Tricky. A bucket-handle tear with the fragment flipped into the notch IS a displaced meniscal fragment, though the word 'displaced' is never dictated, so 'No displaced meniscal fragment.' must be OMITTED. Trap: the 'double PCL sign' is the displaced fragment, not PCL pathology; 'The anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are intact.' must stand. Radiographs this week -> comparison rule not met. 'No bone marrow oedema or fracture.' stands (dictated no bruise or fracture).
